problem: Loopbreaker records what changed in the substrate but not who or what caused it, so a progression cannot be attributed to the ingress that produced it. Writes reach ten tables through twelve distinct write sites - eight direct INSERTs in src/domain.ts, two profile setters in src/db.ts, and two behaviour-status UPDATEs - and none of them carries a source today.
appetite: One instance-carried provenance slice covering every write site on the mutation path, with exact column semantics.
smallest_slice: Carry a provenance triple on the LoopbreakerDb instance set at each ingress, stamp it at all twelve write sites across the ten written tables, define exact trigger_type, triggered_by, and trigger_data values, close the one raw-write bypass, and expose the triple in the substrate readout.
non_goals: A full append-only events log spanning session and workflow planes (stays in Rordi)
Retroactive backfill of a causing ingress that is unknowable for existing rows
Per-MCP-tool granularity, which the shared interleaving handler makes unsafe as ambient per-call state
Provenance on the idempotent migrate() DDL, which writes no rows
Introducing a mutating hook path; hooks are read-only and stay that way in this slice
success_signal: Every one of the twelve write sites - shape_assessments, planning_profiles, issues, behaviors on insert and on both status progressions, planning_findings, planning_review_passes, review_passes, findings, evidence, and waivers - persists a non-null trigger_type and triggered_by with defined values, no mutation path bypasses the stamp, and the substrate readout exposes the triple for every record type that carries it.
reversibility: The columns are additive and nullable. Stop setting provenance at the four ingresses and drop the readout; every gate behaves exactly as before with no data loss and no schema reversal.

risks.risk: Instance-carried provenance identifies the ingress but not the individual MCP tool call.
risks.mitigation: Ingress granularity is the explicit scope and per-tool granularity is a named non-goal, because mcp.ts opens one shared db handle closed over by interleaving async handlers.

risks.risk: Write sites outside the direct INSERTs could be missed, leaving silent gaps.
risks.mitigation: The slice enumerates all twelve sites explicitly, including the two db.ts profile setters and the two behaviour-status UPDATEs, and an enforced behaviour asserts no bypass remains.
